current_date: 26 September 2025 (adopted; went to public consultation 30 June 2025)
current_evidence: The council's 'Validation checklist for planning applications' page states the checklist 'Went to public consultation on 30 June 2025 and adopted on the 26 September 2025'. It is published as web pages: Part 1 national, Part 2 at-a-glance by application type, and Part 3 local requirements (36 items).

issues.detail: The workbook's 'Validation list URL' is not a validation list. It is the 'Non-Statutory Interim Planning Policy Statement: Climate Emergency', a policy statement supplementing the Local Plan. Its only link to validation is the Climate Emergency planning application checklist, which is one of the 36 Part 3 local requirements. Grokbot read the actual Part 3 local requirements page (listed as its 'Planning page') but cited and mined the climate PDF instead.
issues.evidence: PDF title: 'Non-Statutory Interim Planning Policy Statement: Climate Emergency' ... refers to the Council's 'Validation Checklist for planning applications' (s4.1)

issues.detail: A new Local Validation Checklist was adopted on 26 September 2025, after consultation from 30 June to 8 August 2025. The workbook should point to the web-based checklist (Parts 1-3) and not a 2023 policy PDF.
issues.evidence: Validation checklist page: 'Went to public consultation on 30 June 2025 and adopted on the 26 September 2025.'

issues.detail: The list date of 2023-02-01 comes from PDF metadata (CreationDate) of the climate policy statement. That document says February 2023 on the cover and 'Published March 2023'. The actual validation checklist was adopted on 26 September 2025.
issues.evidence: Climate PDF back page: 'Published March 2023'; checklist page: 'adopted on the 26 September 2025'

issues.detail: Most Part 3 local requirements are missing. Not captured: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Declaration (new requirement, required for almost all types); Wildlife & Geology Trigger Table (required for householder, full, outline, RM, LBC and hedgerow); Active Travel England toolkit (150+ dwellings, 7,500 sqm+ or 5 ha+); Agricultural Appraisal (new rural workers' dwellings in the countryside); Air Quality Assessment (major development; car parks over 10 spaces; within 20 m of an AQMA; significant traffic change); Carbon Reduction Statement (major); Climate Emergency checklist/statement (all applications); EIA Screening/Scoping; Foul Drainage Assessment FDA1 (non-mains drainage); Heritage Statement; Justification for Works to a Listed Building; Land Contamination Assessment; LVIA/Landscape Proposals; Mineral Resource Assessment (Devon Minerals Plan M2); Nutrient Neutrality (Somerset Levels and Moors Ramsar catchment); Noise Impact Assessment; Planning Statement (major); Pollution Impact Statement; Retail Impact Assessment; Schedule of Works; Statement of Community Involvement; Statutory Definition of a Caravan; Structural Survey; Telecommunications ICNIRP certificate; Tourism/Holiday Lets; Transport Assessment; Travel Plan; Tree Survey and Report (BS 5837); Viability Assessment; Waste Audit Statement (major). Grokbot even listed the Transport Assessment and Air Quality pages in docs_read but captured neither.
issues.evidence: Part 3 local requirements index lists 36 items, e.g. 'Agricultural Appraisal (DM8)', 'Air Quality Assessment (DM3)', 'Carbon Reduction Statement (DM2)', 'Mineral Resource Assessment (M2)', 'Waste Audit Statement (DM4)'

issues.detail: Householder, Outline, Reserved matters, Listed building consent (except a national D&AS), Lawful development cert, Works to trees, Variation of condition s73, Non-material amendment and Permission in principle all show '(none)' or national-only. The adopted Part 2 checklists set local requirements for every one of these. Householder requires the WGTT and AI Declaration, and may require Climate Emergency, D&AS, Ecology, FRA, Heritage, SWDS and Tree Survey. LBC requires WGTT, Heritage Statement, Schedule of Works, Justification and AI Declaration. Outline requires WGTT, BNG and AI Declaration. S73 requires AI Declaration and BNG. LDC, NMA, PiP and TPO works require the AI Declaration. Telecom prior notification requires an ICNIRP statement.
issues.evidence: Part 2 'at a glance': Householder 'Required: Plans and Drawings; WGTT; AI Declaration'; Listed Building Consent 'Required: ... Heritage Statement; Schedule of Works; Justification; AI Declaration'

issues.detail: All but one of the Full planning rows are 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', e.g. Agricultural Land Classification, BNG, Design Code, EV charging, Energy/Sustainability, Parking, Ventilation. Most are drawn from the climate policy statement and are not validation requirements for any application type.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows notes: 'INFERRED: application type not named in extracted text of a general local list; placed under Full planning'

issues.detail: Several triggers are garbled text from the climate checklist table and do not describe the named requirement. 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal', 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' and 'Ventilation / Extraction details' all quote the same CP.3.x checklist rows about food growing, composting and natural ventilation. 'Design Code / Masterplan' quotes a policy-context paragraph with footnote debris. 'Energy / Sustainability Statement' quotes the document's introduction. The real Agricultural Appraisal trigger is new agricultural, forestry or rural occupational dwellings in the countryside (Policy DM8).
issues.evidence: Agricultural appraisal row: 'and composting (agricultural land classification required) Community food growing opportunities ... CP.3.2 Using energy Residential development more efficiently ...'

issues.detail: The BNG trigger is out of date. It says BNG is 'in advance of the mandatory requirement coming into force (expected in the autumn of 2023)'. Statutory BNG now applies, and the adopted checklist lists BNG as required for Outline and S73 and may-be-required for CoU, full, outline and RM. The EV charging and Parking rows quote Building Regulations Part S, which is not a planning validation trigger.
issues.evidence: BNG row: 'be delivering biodiversity net gain in advance of the mandatory requirement coming into force (expected in the autumn of 2023).'

issues.detail: The 'Flood Risk Assessment' row actually quotes the Surface Water Drainage Strategy requirement ('...the following information with regard to surface water drainage must be submitted as part of a major planning application'). The FRA itself is a separate Part 3 item (Policies S1 and S9) and is may-be-required for householder too.

Most tab_items are policy-context prose and footnote debris from the climate PDF, not requirements. Examples: NPPF paragraph references ('While paragraphs 174 and 179 promote...12 NPPF_July_2021.pdf'), the National Model Design Code and UK Climate Change Risk Assessment paragraph, and a URL fragment about nutrient pollution. Also included are process lines ('We will not hold onto invalid applications awaiting reports'), the BNG metric formatting preference, and a sentence fragment ('- how the mitigation will fully offset the impacts on the SPA/SAC;'). The Somerset Levels and Moors Ramsar item is a cut-off CP.6.1 checklist heading ('...(phosphorus nutrient neutrality): 1.').
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'Neutrality, Support and Funding government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1061531/Chief_Planner_Letter_about_nutrient_pollution___March_2022.pdf 22 23 24 25 21 12 Future National and Local Policy Context...'

issues.detail: Grokbot's 'Planning page' URL uses the old path (/validation-checklist-for-planning-applications-content/validation-checklist-part-3-local-requirements-1/). The current checklist hub is /residents/planning/validation-checklist-for-planning-applications, linking Parts 1-3.
issues.evidence: Hub page links Part 1, Part 2 'at a glance' and Part 3 local requirements

summary: Grokbot cited the 2023 Climate Emergency policy statement PDF instead of Mid Devon's validation checklist. The checklist is web-based (Parts 1-3) and was adopted on 26 September 2025. As a result almost all 36 Part 3 local requirements are missing, every non-Full application type wrongly shows '(none)', and the captured items are mostly garbled policy prose.
